instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Help Me Keep This Quiet
cards.instruction: Get someone to help contain a secret without first revealing its full risk or purpose.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've slipped this envelope under the hamper like you. Out of sight. Keep it there when Mum comes in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's a folded napkin to stop the hamper rocking. Mum asked me to unpack it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Steady first, then. Put the envelope in your pocket while you unpack.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll end up taking it home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Perfect. Keep it there; I'll explain when she stops asking where it is.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're whispering too. Good, you know who we're keeping this from. Hold this cupboard key until tomorrow; don't tell your flatmate.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm hoarse. Tell me what's in the cupboard before I agree.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Save your voice. Nothing alive. Can you keep the key just for tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you collect it before she gets home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed. Text me when she leaves work. Just 'key', please.

cards.title: Not Until You Explain
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until they account for one contradiction, omission, or suspicious change in their story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There, both curtains shut. I saw you start; a private talk is just what we need. You said work kept you till six. Why's this taxi receipt timed five?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm closing up to catch the last bus. I'll explain tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: All ready, then. I'll drive you. What happened to that hour?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I left at five and stopped somewhere before coming home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sit down and tell me where. I'll drive you after you've explained that stop.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've clipped the Friday booking like you. Confirmed copies together. Why does this other page say our wedding's on Monday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The clip holds cancelled versions. Monday was cheaper. Sign the new page; I'm late for work.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Old copies together, yes. Stay while I read this. You told me Friday was confirmed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It was. I moved it after we sent the invitations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then explain when you planned to tell the Friday guests. Work will have to wait for that answer.

cards.title: Apologize for the Lie
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that the concealment or misdirection mattered, even if the underlying choice was defensible.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded my end of the banner like yours. Ready to hang. Did you tell everyone else a different party time?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The party's cancelled. I'm folding it away. I didn't tell you because I didn't want to upset you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Away neatly, then. You let me arrive with a cake; that hurt more than a cancellation message.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm sorry the party didn't happen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can accept cancelling. Say you're sorry I had to find out with a cake in my hands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've folded the adoption leaflet to the photo like you. Just the useful page. What happened to our sofa?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He chews furniture; that's on the back. I hid it because he needed a home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Back page, yes. Admit that hiding it changed my yes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy another sofa.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Thank you. Before we feed him another one, say I should have had both pages.

cards.title: Approve the Cover Story
cards.instruction: Get someone to endorse an explanation that protects the plan, reputation, or people involved.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my name under yours on the hall form. Approved users. Back me when I say we opened the cupboard for chairs; we need the hall again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the list of people who opened it without permission. Chairs don't fit in that cupboard.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Everyone accounted for, then. We were looking for folding stools. Can you back that?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if you admit you borrowed the caretaker's key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrowed his key to check for extra seating. Will you sign that explanation with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've underlined 'delivery delay' in green like you. Approved copy. Will you back it in the newsletter so our volunteer isn't blamed for the melted cake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Green means check the claim. She delivered on time; we left it by the radiator.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Checked, then: 'storage problem'. Will you approve that explanation?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only if we promise a refund.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: 'Storage problem; we'll refund you.' Can I put your name under that?

cards.title: You Handle the Evidence
cards.instruction: Make someone else take responsibility for the evidence, loose end, or difficult follow-up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put the raffle cashbox under the desk like yours. Secure storage. Keep it here until the treasurer comes; I can't explain the broken lock.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine's an empty box. I moved it to make room for a chair. This office doesn't lock either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Room cleared, then. Take the cashbox home and hand it to her tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She'll want me to count it with her.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Do the count and explain the lock. I'll give you the snapped key too, so you have everything she'll ask about.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've starred the magician's number like you. Paid and filed. You can explain the missing receipt to the treasurer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Stars mean I haven't called yet. You paid him; I only found the number.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Next call ready, then. Ring him for a duplicate; you've got his details.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He only sends duplicates when the treasurer emails him directly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Draft her email and get her to send it. Copy yourself in so you can chase the answer.
